steps.text: Convection is how heat moves through liquids and gases — the fluid itself carries the heat. Let's watch it.
Turn on the heat under the water and watch the particles.
Hot water is lighter, so it rises; cooler water is heavier, so it sinks. This sets up a loop called a convection current.
Hot rises, cold sinks, round and round. That's convection — the same reason warm air rises in a room.
